correctness.rationale: For each real midpoint eigenvalue mu in (-1,1), the complete two-index AR(1) covariance convolution is absolutely summable and equals q(1+mu*rho)/[(1-mu^2)(1-mu*rho)]. Differentiation gives a strictly positive sum of curvature terms, hence the unique optimum/boundary criterion. The mixed-sign two-mode stationary root and its exact radicals have been reconstructed, and the left/right noise gains are exactly I versus (I+hA/2)^-1. The finite-horizon O(h^2) RMS bound follows from the AR(1) Toeplitz norm and h^(5/2) scale. The standalone standard-library verifier passed 1,080 supporting checks on the actual newly written code; finite checks supplement rather than certify the universal proof.

value.rationale: When choosing temporal dependence in probabilistic midpoint perturbations, the optimizer is a well-motivated fixed-marginal numerical error-floor problem. The result supplies a dimension-general strictly convex spectral decision rule, a sharp two-mode phase interval, and an exact nontrivial-constrained example where the optimal temporal correlation changes sign solely by moving noise from the completed numerical state to the equation right-hand side. This rejects the tempting universal recommendation that one sign of time correlation always reduces artificial numerical spread, while preserving second-order finite-horizon accuracy. The benefit is a precise mathematical noise-design boundary, not a claim of calibrated uncertainty quantification.
